doc: Denon/Marantz telnet control protocol grammar.
This data file is the ONLY place that contains fixed wire tokens (such as
PSBAS for bass or the enum values OFF/LOW/MID/HI/AUTO). It exists because a
receiver does not publish its own wire vocabulary: it describes controls by
functional names (ToneControl, DynamicCompression, ...) and by display names,
ranges, steps and option labels, but never says 'bass is sent as PSBAS'. That
linkage is the Denon protocol itself and is identical across all Denon and
Marantz models.
Everything device specific (which controls actually exist, their display
names, numeric ranges, option labels, the channel list, the source list and
renames, visibility) is discovered at runtime from the receiver and is NEVER
stored here. The engine builds an entity for a control only when the receiver
advertises the matching capability AND this profile knows how to speak to it.
For enum controls, 'values' lists the wire tokens in the canonical protocol
order. The engine pairs them, by position, with the ordered display labels the
receiver publishes. When the counts differ it falls back to the wire tokens as
labels so a mismatch can never cause a wrong command to be sent.

sound_mode_wire_overrides.doc: Deterministic display-name -> MS wire token map for modes whose wire token differs from the upper-cased display name. These tokens were observed live from the receiver (it reports them via MS). For every other mode the upper-cased display name is used.

sound_mode_genre_commands.doc: How to switch the receiver to a sound mode genre group. Keyed by the genre code the receiver uses (from OPSMLALL/SSSMG); the value is the MS command token. Verified live: MOVIE/MUSIC/GAME work; the Pure group needs 'PURE DIRECT' (plain 'PURE' does not). This is fixed protocol grammar; the codes and display names still come from the device.

listed_sound_modes.doc: Sound modes of receivers that do not list them over telnet (OPSML and OPSMLALL get no answer, AVR-X2000 and older). Keyed by the function name the receiver lists in Deviceinfo.xml; the value is the MS wire token. From the MS command table of the AVR-X2000/E400 protocol (v03, 2013) and the AVR-1713, AVR-1912 and AVR-2113 documents; only modes whose function name the receiver lists are offered. PURE in Deviceinfo has no MS command of its own (PURE DIRECT is listed separately), so it is left out.

source_names.doc: Names for inputs the receiver lists without a name: SSFUN names the user's inputs only, SSSOD lists the network services, tuner and network input by code (an AVR-X2000: IRADIO, SERVER, LASTFM; an AVR-X2600H: TUNER, NET). The names are the receiver's own from its Deviceinfo.xml (DefaultName of the AVR-X2000 recording: Internet Radio, Media Server, Favorites, iPod/USB, Flickr) and the services' own spelling, in title case for NETWORK and TUNER. A name the receiver reports always wins.

netaudio.doc: Now playing and transport over telnet, for receivers without HEOS (AVR-X2000 and older). NSE asks for the on-screen list (NSE0-NSE8, UTF-8): line 0 starts with 'Now Playing' while a track plays, lines 1, 2 and 4 hold title, artist and album after one flag byte. NS9A-NS9E play, pause, stop, skip forward and back. The cover is served under art_path on the goform port. From the AVR-X2000/E400 (v03), AVR-1912/2112CI, AVR-1913/2113CI and 2015 X-series documents and the denonavr library (input.py). TFAN? and TFANNAME? give the tuner frequency (6 digits, below 050000 FM in MHz x 100, else AM in kHz x 100) and station name.
netaudio.position_doc: Line 5 holds the elapsed time while a track plays: '00:11 100%' in the AVR-X2000/E400 (v03) document, '   03:36 ' from an AVR-X2000 (counting up every 5 s, '00:00' at a track change). The percentage, where it comes, gives the duration.

tuner_presets.doc: TPAN? gives the recalled preset (TPAN01, TPANOFF when none); TPAN<code> recalls one, TPANUP and TPANDOWN step through them, only while the source is the tuner. 56 presets, numbered 01-56 in the 2015 X-series document and confirmed by an AVR-X2600H (TPAN01).
The AVR-X2000/E400 (v03) and AVR-1912/2112CI documents name the 56 presets A1-G8 (eight per letter); the 2113CI document (v04, May 2013) and the 2015 X-series document use 01-56.

information.doc: General > Information page of the setup interface: Firmware/Version (build code) and Firmware/DTSVersion, the DTS decoder (LaserGuruGuy's recordings: 4.30.10.15 on an AVC-X3900H).

hdmi_setup.doc: HDMI setup as the receiver stores it, one line per item, ended by SSHOS END; pushed on a change and with each read of the video setup pages (LaserGuruGuy, AVR-X3600H/AVC-X3900H). A grayed item shows in the menu the value HDMI Control imposes; this line keeps the item's own setting. Older receivers answer only SSHOSALS (auto lip sync).

audio_menu_status.doc: One digit per Audio setup menu item, the setup page's display minus 1: 0 hidden, 1 grayed, 2 settable, in this order; spare digits follow. Pushed when it changes, for example with the sound mode (LaserGuruGuy, AVR-X3600H/AVC-X3900H). A setting whose item is hidden or grayed is refused before it is sent. The digits and their order are his; which settings belong to an item (controls) and that the receiver keeps a setting of a grayed item are this integration's reading, not yet confirmed.

distance.doc: Speaker distance grammar. The wire value is the distance times 'divisor' (e.g. '0310' = 3.10 m). Range/step are Denon protocol facts, not device reported.

doc: Speaker crossover grammar. Per speaker group the wire value is the
frequency in Hz, zero padded to 'width' digits (e.g. '080' = 80 Hz).
The allowed frequencies are a DISCRETE, non-uniform set, so this is a
select, not a min/max/step number. This is a FIXED Denon protocol
constant (the same crossover grid across the lineup), so it lives here
like every other enum's wire values - not device-variable, no runtime
fetch. The receiver reports its CURRENT crossover per group over telnet
(SSCFR) but never enumerates the allowed set on any channel; the set here
was verified live (a telnet accept-probe and the web config's
SelectableValue both agreed on it exactly).
Manual graphic equaliser grammar. FIXED protocol constant, like the
crossover grid above: the nine ISO-octave bands (63 Hz..16 kHz) and the
dB range (-20.0..+6.0, step 0.5) are the same across the Denon/Marantz
lineup, so they are hardcoded here (and verified against the device), NOT
fetched at runtime. This is deliberate for robustness: the band metadata
must not depend on the goform Deviceinfo or the setup web interface,
neither of which is in the official protocol document and the web UI can
change on a firmware redesign. Only the live per-band VALUES have no other
source; they are read/written through the setup config API on port 10443
(non-disruptive): read is GET /ajax/<config_section>/get_config?type=
<config_type>; write is ALSO a GET, /ajax/<config_section>/set_config?
type=<config_type>&data=<url-encoded XML> (a POST is rejected). A band
write must send the whole AdjustEQ block (Channel + all bands), not one
band. Each band's XML tag is band_tag_prefix +
the band label with spaces removed (e.g. '1 kHz' -> 'Eq1kHz'); each wire
value is the gain in dB times db_divisor (e.g. -110 = -11.0 dB). Speaker
selection applies one curve to all speakers, the L/R pair, or each
channel. Editing requires MultEQ off and the graphic EQ enabled.

video_web.doc: Video setup menu settings that have NO telnet token, read/written via the setup config API (/ajax/video/{get,set}_config). type=1 is the availability map; each control names its config type and XML tag. On/off wire values are Denon's SETTING_ON=1/SETTING_OFF=2 except OSD Info which uses VIDEO_SETTING On=1/Off=0. Option maps + the pass-through source values are the receiver's own (from the setup UI).

collections.doc: 4K/8K signal format per input (Web Control generation, AVC-X3900H; recorded by LaserGuruGuy). Custom (3) only where the input reports MaxResolution 1. Written as <Format index="slot">id</Format>, as the receiver's own page does; not yet confirmed on a receiver.
HDCP version per input (Web Control generation). Custom (4) only where the input reports Limit 1. Written as <Value index="slot">id</Value>; not yet confirmed on a receiver.

speakers_web.doc: Speaker-setup settings with no telnet token, read/written via the /ajax speakers config API. Amp Assign (AssignMode, config type=2) is DEVICE-DRIVEN: the valid modes depend on the receiver's queried AmpType, so the option list is keyed by AmpType in amptype_options (extracted from the setup UI's getAmpAssignList, covering every Denon/Marantz amp type - not X3600H-specific). Read type=2 gives AmpType (selects the list) + AssignMode (current value); set is a field-only /ajax write <AssignMode>N</AssignMode>. Values are numeric AssignMode ids; labels are the receiver's own (e.g. 6='7.1ch + Front B').

collections.doc: Speaker layout, the Web Control successor of Amp Assign: item 1 is the assign mode, its <List> the modes this receiver allows. Written as <Config index="1">id</Config> (LaserGuruGuy verified it on an AVC-X3900H). A change resets the positions' choices and front speaker A/B, so it is staged and applied by a button, with a repair to restore.
The choice per speaker position (<Config>) with the position's own allowed list. Written only to restore what a layout change reset.
How a speaker position is connected now (Conn): speakers and pre-out, or pre-out only. Read only; positions named as LaserGuruGuy found them in the receiver's web app.

doc: Maps the receiver's speaker group codes (from the SSSPC introspection) to
channel codes, so only speakers that are actually configured get channel
entities. Which groups are present is discovered from SSSPC; this map is
just the fixed protocol grammar linking a group to its channels. A group
is treated as absent when its latest presence or size value is an absent
token. The subwoofer is NON/1SP/2SP on receivers with two
subwoofer outputs and YES/NO on others: an AVR-X2000 and an AVR-X2600H
(3.139.175) answer 'SSSPCSWF YES', and the AVR-X2000 'SSSPCSWF NO' once
its subwoofer was set to None.

sizes.doc: Speaker size wire tokens for the regular (non-count) groups, exposed as a select. LAR=Large, SMA=Small; the absent_token (NON) means no speaker. The count groups (subwoofer, surround back) report presence/count tokens instead and are not size-selectable. Set via 'SSSPC<GROUP> <token>' (verified live: read -> set -> restore).

count_groups.doc: A count group reports up to two values per answer: its presence or size, and its count (count_tokens). The AVR-X2000 and AVR-X2600H answer 'SSSPCSBK NON' and then 'SSSPCSBK 2SP': no surround back, the count setting kept. Each kind replaces only its own earlier value. Every subwoofer value is a count.

doc: How zones are addressed on the wire. The NUMBER and names of zones are
discovered from the receiver (DeviceZones); only the addressing grammar is
fixed here. The main zone uses the core controls (ZM/MV/MU/SI). Every
additional zone N uses the prefix 'Z<N>' (Z2, Z3, ...), which is overloaded
for power, volume, mute and source; the parser disambiguates by content.

source_names.doc: One line per input: 'SSFUN<CODE> <display name>'. Provides the SI source code and the (possibly renamed) display name.

source_visibility.doc: One line per input: 'SSSOD<CODE> USE|DEL'. Marks which sources the user kept visible.

channel_levels.doc: One line per configured channel: 'SSLEV<CODE> <level>' terminated by 'SSLEV END'. Reveals which channels are actually configured.

channel_distances.doc: One line per channel: 'SSSDE<CODE> <value>' (value = distance x divisor) terminated by 'SSSDE END'. 'SSSDESTP' carries the unit and is ignored.

speaker_config.doc: One line per speaker group with its size/presence setting. Settable per group via 'SSSPC<GROUP> <token>' (see speakers.sizes for the size tokens).

crossover.doc: One line per speaker group: 'SSCFR<GROUP> <Hz>' terminated by 'SSCFR END'. 'SSCFR IDV' (the crossover mode: Individual) has no value and is ignored; 'SSCFRALL <Hz>' is the value used when all speakers share one crossover and is also ignored (per-group values are authoritative). This gives the CURRENT crossover per group; the selectable value set is the fixed protocol constant in grammar.crossover.

sound_mode_group.doc: Reports the receiver's current sound mode genre group directly (MOV/MUS/GAM/PUR).

quick_select_names.doc: Main zone quick select preset names, one per line ('SSQSNZMAQS<n> <name>'), terminated by 'SSQSNZMA END'.

quick_select_blocks.doc: Newer receivers (AVC-X3900H, recorded by LaserGuruGuy/denon_avr) answer no SSQSNZMA ? but name each preset in a block: SSQS<n>QSN <name>, one line per stored item (SRC, VOL, SDM ...), SSQS<n> END. Asked only while no SSQSNZMA name has come; only the name is used.

marantz.doc: Marantz FY20 AVR control protocol (2019): Smart Select MSSMART1-5, MSSMART<n> MEMORY, MSSMART0, MSSMART ?; recorded Marantz Deviceinfo files from SR6011 on name it Smart Select.

quick_select.doc: Currently recalled main zone quick select preset number (0 = none/modified).

sound_mode_list.doc: OPSMLALL lists every available sound mode across all genres (Movie/Music/Game/Pure), one per line, terminated by 'OPSMLALL END'. Used for the full flat set and the per genre groups.

current_sound_modes.doc: OPSML lists the modes actually selectable in the CURRENT context/group, terminated by 'OPSML END'. Context aware: includes modes OPSMLALL omits (such as Auto) and marks the selected mode. Drives the sound mode select for the active group.

receiver_type.doc: How the hardware/receiver type (device hw_version) is classified, matching the official denonavr library: it is the receiver TYPE (avr / avr-x / avr-x-2016), NOT the Deviceinfo Gen code. The library picks it by which port serves Deviceinfo.xml (80 -> avr-x, 8080 -> avr-x-2016) gated by an 'is AVR-X' test; so does this integration: an AVR-X device is 'avr_x_type' on 8080 and 'avr_x_port80_type' on 80, anything else is 'default_type'. A device is AVR-X when its CommApiVers matches commapi_pattern OR its ModelName matches avr_x_pattern (both regexes verbatim from the library). Read from the equipment, works for any model, no Gen map.

sample_rate.name: Sample Rate
sample_rate.doc: Sample rate token such as '48K'. 'NON' means no active signal.

decoder.name: Decoder
decoder.doc: Active decoder/audio format, for example 'PCM' (space padded).

mode_info.name: Mode Info
mode_info.doc: Informational mode string, for example 'Stereo' (space padded).

refresh.doc: Coalesced re-query groups. When a pushed line's prefix matches an entry in 'on', that group's 'queries' are re-sent after 'debounce' seconds; a burst of matching events collapses into a single re-query. This keeps derived state the receiver does not push on every relevant change in sync: the sound mode lists follow a signal change; the audio information (format/decoder/rate/mode) and the channel/speaker layout follow a sound mode or source change, which the receiver reports (MS/SI) but without re-sending the dependent state.

speaker_preset.doc: A speaker preset holds the whole speaker setup (layout, distances, levels, crossovers, graphic EQ; seen by LaserGuruGuy/denon_avr on an AVC-X3900H): switching it asks the speaker lines again and reads the setup interface again. Only on a change of the value, never for its first report after connecting (the resync asks for everything).

buttons.doc: Command buttons: name -> telnet command. CVZRL is documented in the 2015 X-series document; NSRBT comes from the denonavr library. Neither has a query, so they start disabled on every receiver.

remote.doc: Remote entity commands: name -> telnet command. Cursor, enter, return, option, info, channel level menu and the setup menu, documented in the AVR-X2000, AVR-x1x13, AVR-x1x12 and 2015 X-series protocol documents (MNOPT, MNINF and MNCHL not in the 2012 one). The setup menu (MNMEN ON / OFF) is confirmed on an AVR-X2600H, which echoes it and answers MNMEN? (tests/fixtures/command_test); the cursor, enter, return, option, info and channel level commands are not yet tried on a receiver.

system_power.doc: System standby power. Distinct from the main zone power.

main_power.doc: Main zone power. Also on the media player; exposed as a switch too. State comes from the ZM event (mirrored into values).

main_volume.doc: Master volume. Two/three digit half step scale, 80 == 0 dB reference.

main_mute.doc: Main zone mute. Also on the media player; exposed as a switch too with a speaker/mute icon. State comes from the MU event (mirrored into values).

main_source.doc: Main zone input source. Codes and names are discovered via SSFUN/SSSOD.

sound_mode.doc: Surround / sound mode. Selectable values are learned from what the receiver reports.

bass.doc: Tone control bass. Level, 50 == 0 dB. The range comes from the receiver where it publishes one: whole dB on an AVR-X2600H and an AVC-X3700H recording; the AVR-X2600H ignored a half step (PSBAS 505) in the command test. Without one (AVR-X2000, receivers before 2016) -6 to +6 dB in whole dB, as every protocol document from 2011 to 2015 gives it (44 to 56); an AVR-X2000 ignored a half step as well.

treble.doc: Tone control treble. Level, 50 == 0 dB. The range comes from the receiver where it publishes one: whole dB on an AVR-X2600H and an AVC-X3700H recording; the AVR-X2600H ignored a half step (PSTRE 505) in the command test. Without one (AVR-X2000, receivers before 2016) -6 to +6 dB in whole dB, as every protocol document from 2011 to 2015 gives it (44 to 56); an AVR-X2000 ignored a half step as well.

lfe.doc: LFE level, 0 down to -10 dB, sent as two digits without a sign: PSLFE 00 is 0 dB, PSLFE 10 is -10 dB (AVR-X2000/E400 v03, AVR-1713, AVR-2113CI and 2015 X-series documents). The receiver does not publish this range (its LFE block is empty), so the protocol defined range is given here as a fallback.

graphic_eq.name: Enabled
graphic_eq.doc: Graphic EQ on/off (telnet PSGEQ). The per-band values are on the setup config API, not telnet; this on/off switch lives on the EQ sub-device with the band numbers. Named 'Enabled' so it reads as 'Graphic EQ Enabled', not doubled.

room_size.doc: Audyssey DSX room size. Wire tokens from the Denon protocol document; labels from Deviceinfo when published. Candidate: silent on the X3600H '?' probe (a no-op/inapplicable state also yields silence), gated on the advertised RoomSize capability.

dialog_level.doc: Center level adjust (the receiver's DialogLevel function, named Center Level Adjust in its Deviceinfo). PSCLV <nn>, 38 to 62 with half steps, 50 = 0 dB (level kind), per Denon's FY21 AVR protocol table (v02, 2020) for the AVR-X2700H to X4700H and S960H. Range derives from the device's DialogLevel block. An AVR-X2600H and an AVR-X3600H left PSDIL ? unanswered. The CY2022 table (v02) marks PSCLV for none of its models.

older.doc: PSDIL <nn> in the 2015 X-series document; the AVR-X2000 left PSDIL ? unanswered.

headphone_eq.doc: Headphone EQ on/off (PSHEQ, in Denon's FY21 table and the 2015 X-series document). No recorded Deviceinfo and no Denon app names a HeadphoneEq function, so it is shown when the receiver answers the query at setup: the AVR-X2600H answers OFF, the AVR-X2000 does not answer.

auto_lip_sync.doc: Auto lip sync (automatic A/V delay). An AVR-X2600H (3.139.175) answers SSALS ? with SSALSSET ON, SSALSDSP OFF and SSALSVAL 000, and has no SSHOSALS (neither SSHOSALS ? nor a line in SSHOS ?); SSALSSET is read as the setting. Writing 'SSALSSET ON|OFF' is in no document; an AVR-X2600H took both in its command test. Receivers on port 80 report it as SSHOSALS in the HDMI setup list instead (older variant). Gated on the advertised AutoLipSync capability or an answer.

older.doc: AVR-X2000: SSHOSALS ON inside SSHOS ?, no answer to SSHOSALS ?; SSHOSALS OFF confirmed in its command test.

variants.doc: AVC-X3900H (3.139.174, recorded by LaserGuruGuy/denon_avr): OPALSSET ON, OPALSDSP ON and OPALSVAL 000, also pushed with an input change; no SSALS. The answered prefix is also written (OPALSSET ON|OFF), not yet tried on a receiver.

2011.doc: AVR-1912/2112CI document (2011): PSDYNVOL NGT, EVE, DAY, no off; the AVR-1713 and AVR-2113CI documents already use OFF, LIT, MED, HEV. For the receivers without Deviceinfo.xml.

cinema_eq.doc: Cinema EQ. Note the embedded '.' in the wire token.

before_x.doc: Before 2014, outside the AVR-X and AVR-E series: PSRSTR MODE1, MODE2, MODE3, OFF in the AVR-1912/2112CI (2011), AVR-1713 and AVR-2113CI documents. The receivers' own Deviceinfo.xml lists MODE1 as High, MODE2 as Middle and MODE3 as Low (recorded AVR-1713, AVR-3313), as Denon's 2015 document pairs them (HI = MODE1, LOW = MODE3).

marantz.doc: Marantz receivers from level 0300 name M-DAX Restorer in Deviceinfo.xml (FuncName Restorer, DispName M-DAX: recorded SR6011, SR6012, NR1609, AV7703). Marantz's 2019 document has no PSRSTR, only PSMDAX, and the manufacturer's apps send M-DAX as PSMDAX to every Marantz receiver above level 100 (AV7005 and SR7005 excepted). So the Restorer gate is M-DAX there; the control is kept only for a receiver that answers PSRSTR ?.

restorer.doc: Restorer (compressed audio restoration). Denon FY21 command list: PSRSTR OFF, LOW, MED, HI and PSRSTR ?; answered by an AVR-X2000 and an AVR-X2600H.

subwoofer_level.doc: Subwoofer level, half step, 50 == 0 dB. The dB range is discovered from the receiver's SubwooferLevel block.

subwoofer_2_level.doc: Level of subwoofer 2, as subwoofer 1. PSSWL ? answers it next to PSSWL when the subwoofer is set up (LaserGuruGuy/denon_avr saw 'PSSWL2 59'; the recorded AVC-X3900H reports SSLEVSW2 to SSLEVSW4). Not yet tried on a receiver by this integration.

subwoofer_3_level.doc: Level of subwoofer 3, as subwoofer 1. PSSWL ? answers it next to PSSWL when the subwoofer is set up (LaserGuruGuy/denon_avr saw 'PSSWL2 59'; the recorded AVC-X3900H reports SSLEVSW2 to SSLEVSW4). Not yet tried on a receiver by this integration.

subwoofer_4_level.doc: Level of subwoofer 4, as subwoofer 1. PSSWL ? answers it next to PSSWL when the subwoofer is set up (LaserGuruGuy/denon_avr saw 'PSSWL2 59'; the recorded AVC-X3900H reports SSLEVSW2 to SSLEVSW4). Not yet tried on a receiver by this integration.

volume_scale.name: Volume Scale
volume_scale.doc: Master volume display scale: Relative (dB around 0, e.g. -79.5..+18.0) or Absolute (0..98). SSVCTZMADIS (verified live). Core-scoped, no FuncName, parsed explicitly.

volume_limit.name: Volume Limit
volume_limit.doc: Maximum master volume limit. SSVCTZMALIM; the numeric values are the master-volume scale (060=-20 dB, 070=-10 dB, 080=0 dB). Verified live. Core-scoped, no FuncName, parsed explicitly.

muting_level.name: Muting Level
muting_level.doc: Attenuation applied when muted: Full or -40 dB. SSVCTZMAMLV (MUT / 040; -20 dB is not offered on this model). Verified live. Core-scoped, no FuncName, parsed explicitly.

all_zone_stereo.name: All Zone Stereo
all_zone_stereo.doc: All Zone Stereo: play the main zone audio in stereo across every zone. Set via 'MNZST ON|OFF' (verified live). Core-scoped (no Deviceinfo FuncName), parsed explicitly. Asked as 'MNZST?' without a space, the form Denon's FY21 AVR protocol table gives; 'MNZST ?' got no answer from an AVR-X2600H or an AVR-X3600H. As a fallback the on/off state is derived from the sound mode (MS reports 'ALL ZONE STEREO' when active, verified live) - this gives a known state (single toggle, not two buttons) from the resync MS? onwards; the MNZST echo/push updates it immediately on change. An AVR-X2600H (3.139.175) took 'MNZST ON' sent right after a MultEQ change and back, then answered nothing for the rest of a command test; the same command after other settings came and went normally.

subwoofer_mode.name: Subwoofer Mode
subwoofer_mode.doc: Subwoofer mode: LFE only, or LFE + Main (the mains' low frequencies are also sent to the subwoofer). Verified live read/write via 'SSSWM <token>'. Core-scoped: it has no Deviceinfo FuncName, so it is always queried and parsed explicitly; labels are given here as there is no device option list.

front_speaker.name: Front Speaker
front_speaker.doc: Front speaker terminal selection (Denon PSFRONT SPA/SPB/A+B). NOTE the query is 'PSFRONT?' with NO space (unlike other PS controls); the set is 'PSFRONT <token>' with a space. Only applies when Amp Assign is set to Front B; the receiver reports/accepts it only in that mode, so the state may be unknown otherwise. Verified live: read via 'PSFRONT?' and set 'PSFRONT A+B' echoed.

lpf_for_lfe.name: LPF for LFE
lpf_for_lfe.doc: Low-pass filter for the LFE channel (Denon SSLFL, 3-digit Hz, query 'SSLFL ?' WITH space). Verified live read/write (080<->090, reversible). The frequency set is the standard LFE LPF range, confirmed by the /ajax speakers type=17 SelectableValue list (80..250 Hz).

zone2_sleep_timer.doc: Zone 2 sleep timer in minutes (Z2SLP, 001-120, OFF). AVR-X2000/E400 protocol v03 and the 2015 X-series document; answered by an AVR-X2000 and an AVR-X2600H (capability checks).

zone2_auto_standby.doc: Zone 2 auto standby (Z2STBY 2H/4H/8H/OFF), from the 2015 X-series document. Answered by an AVR-X2600H; the AVR-X2000 does not answer it.

zone2_hdmi_audio.doc: Zone 2 HDMI audio: passed through or as PCM (Z2HDA THR/PCM), from the 2015 X-series document (AVR-X3200W, AVR-X4200W). An AVR-X2000 answers Z2HDA THR; an AVR-X2600H does not answer. A receiver that does not answer probably plays no HDMI input in Zone 2, so its HDMI inputs start deselected when Zone 2's inputs are asked for. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

marantz.doc: Marantz FY20 AVR control protocol (2019): Z2SMART1-5, Z2SMART0, Z2SMART ?.

zone2_quick_select.doc: Zone 2 quick select recall (Z2QUICK1-5; Z2QUICK0 when none is active). AVR-X2000/E400 protocol v03 and the 2015 X-series document; Z2QUICK ? answered by an AVR-X2000 and an AVR-X2600H. Offered as many as the main zone has (SSQSNZMA).

zone2_channel_level_fl.doc: Zone 2 front left level (Z2CVFL, 38-62, 50 == 0 dB; whole dB only, as Denon's FY21 table gives it). AVR-X2000/E400 protocol v03 and the 2015 X-series document; answered by an AVR-X2000 and an AVR-X2600H.

zone2_channel_level_fr.doc: Zone 2 front right level (Z2CVFR), as the front left.

sleep_timer.doc: Sleep timer in minutes ('OFF' when disabled). The receiver does not publish a range (its SleepTimer block is empty), so the protocol defined range is given here as a fallback.

dts_neural_x.doc: DTS Neural:X upmixer. Verified live (PSNEURAL ON/OFF). Only applies to compatible content.

low_frequency_containment.doc: Low Frequency Containment. Verified live (PSLFC ON/OFF).

effect_level.doc: DSP effect level (matrix/DSP sound modes). Verified live (PSEFF). The receiver publishes only step/default, so 0-15 is the protocol fallback range. Only applies in DSP modes.

containment_amount.doc: LFC containment amount. Verified live (PSCNTAMT). The range is the one Deviceinfo.xml publishes (MinValue/MaxValue, 1-7 on the AVC-X3700H); 1-7 (01-07) from Denon's FY21 AVR protocol table (v02, 2020) where it publishes none. Applies when LFC is on.

older.doc: 0-200 ms in the AVR-X2000/E400 (v03) and 2015 X-series documents.

audio_delay.doc: Audio delay in milliseconds. Denon's FY21 table gives 0-500 ms for receivers from 2016 on; the older documents give 0-200 ms (older variant). Where Deviceinfo.xml publishes the range (AudioDelay/Adjust from 2016, AudioDelay itself on the AVR-X2100W), that range is used.

dialog_control.doc: Dialog Control level 0-6, or the range Deviceinfo.xml publishes (MinValue/MaxValue).

dimmer.doc: Front panel display brightness. Wire token for Dark is DAR (verified live; 'DRK' is rejected). Labels come from the device when published, otherwise these.

video_mode.doc: Video processing mode. Wire values verified live (AUTO/GAME/MOVI); labels come from Deviceinfo. Only changeable with an active video signal. BYP from Denon's 2020 command list (VSVPMBYP, not on every model); offered only where Deviceinfo.xml lists Bypass (AVR-X2600H, AVC-X3700H, AVC-A10H; not the AVR-X4300H).

picture_mode.doc: Picture mode (Denon protocol PV<mode>). Tokens from the official protocol doc. The 'PV' prefix is shared with the video-adjust settings (PVBR/PVCN/...), so exact_enum makes this control claim only the picture-mode value tokens. Device reports PVSTM (Stream).

2013.doc: AVR-X2000/E400 protocol v03 (2013): two digits, 44-56, 50 == 0 (-6..+6); three digits from the 2014 documents on.

contrast.doc: Picture contrast (Denon PVCN). 3-digit wire, 050 == 0, range -50..+50. Availability comes from the /ajax PictureAdjust menu (feature injected at discovery); writes require an active HDMI video signal.

2013.doc: AVR-X2000/E400 protocol v03 (2013): two digits, 00-12, 00 == 0; three digits from the 2014 documents on.
AVR-X2000/E400 protocol v03 (2013): two digits, 44-56, 50 == 0 (-6..+6); three digits from the 2014 documents on.

saturation.doc: Picture saturation/chroma (Denon PVST). 3-digit wire, 050 == 0, range -50..+50. The trailing space distinguishes 'PVST ' from the picture-mode tokens PVSTD/PVSTM.

hdmi_video_output.doc: HDMI monitor output selection. Wire values verified live (AUTO/1/2).

aspect_ratio.doc: Video aspect ratio. Wire values verified live (FUL=16:9, NRM=4:3).

hdmi_audio_out.doc: HDMI audio output routing: AMP (the receiver decodes/plays the audio) or TV (HDMI audio passed through to the TV, muting the receiver). Note the trailing space in the prefix ('VSAUDIO <value>'). Read/write verified live via an /ajax cross-check (AMP<->TV flips the receiver's HDMIAudioOut). Labels come from the device when it publishes them, otherwise these.

resolution_hdmi.doc: HDMI output resolution (scaler). Wire tokens from the Denon control protocol (VSSCH<token>); AUTO/48P/10I/72P/10P/10P24/4K verified live read/write. Only settable when Video Conversion is on and the IP scaler is on HDMI (the receiver otherwise rejects it); this is the ResolutionHDMI field the web Output Settings page gates the same way. 'VSSC' (analog) is a separate, hidden path and is not exposed. 8K (VSSCH8K) from Denon's 2020 command list, offered only where Deviceinfo.xml lists it (AVC-X3700H); not yet taken by a receiver.

input_mode.doc: Audio input mode for the current source (how audio is received). This is the eARC/ARC selector for the TV Audio source. EARC verified live (the source stayed locked to the active eARC signal, so the other values could not be cycle-verified); the rest are the documented Denon SD tokens. Order matches the Deviceinfo Input Mode list.

channel_level.doc: Per channel volume trim. Configured channels, their names and their dB ranges are all discovered from the receiver; live trims are read/written via CV<code>.

auto_standby.doc: Auto standby. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands). An AVR-X2600H answers STBY15M and ignored STBY8H in the command test (tests/fixtures/command_test): 2H/4H/8H may be Zone 2 values only; unconfirmed. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

trigger_1.doc: 12 V trigger 1. TR? answers both triggers. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

trigger_2.doc: 12 V trigger 2. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

speaker_preset.doc: Speaker preset. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

bluetooth_transmitter.doc: Bluetooth transmitter. The same prefix also reports the output mode (SP, BT), which this control ignores. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

dialog_enhancer.doc: Dialogue Enhancer. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

imax.doc: IMAX Enhanced: AUTO, ON or OFF as Denon's FY21 AVR protocol table (v02, 2020) gives them for the AVR-X3700H and up; the denonavr library knows AUTO and OFF only, and the CY2022 table (v02) drops ON for the AVR-X3800H and up. Not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

imax_audio.doc: IMAX audio settings. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

imax_hpf.doc: IMAX high-pass filter, zero padded to three digits as the library sends it. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

imax_lpf.doc: IMAX low-pass filter, zero padded. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

imax_subwoofer.doc: IMAX subwoofer mode. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

imax_subwoofer_output.doc: IMAX subwoofer output, L+M or LFE, in Denon's CY2022 AVR protocol table (v02) for the AVR-X3800H and up and in the denonavr library; not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

auro_matic_preset.doc: Auro-Matic 3D preset. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

auro_matic_strength.doc: Auro-Matic 3D strength 1-16 (2015 X-series document); two digits assumed. Not taken from Deviceinfo.xml: the AVC-A10H publishes 0-15, the AVR-X4300H 1-16, and as with Effect Level the published start may not be what the wire takes. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

auro_3d_mode.doc: Auro-3D mode. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

dirac_filter.doc: Dirac Live filter slot. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

mdax.doc: M-DAX (Marantz): OFF, LOW, MID, HI and PSMDAX ? for all five models of the Marantz FY20 AVR control protocol (Ver 3, 2019), and the Denon and Marantz AVR Remote apps (3.13.4) send the same four values; the denonavr library sends MED, which that table does not have. Not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

dac_filter.doc: DAC filter (Marantz). Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

illumination.doc: Illumination (Marantz). The ILB event broke the official integration's setup with HA 2026.2. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

tactile_transducer.doc: Tactile transducer. SSTTR ? also answers SSTTRLEV and SSTTRLPF and ends with SSTTR END. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

tactile_transducer_level.doc: Tactile transducer level, half step like the channel levels (50 = 0 dB); range from the channel level table. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

tactile_transducer_lpf.doc: Tactile transducer low-pass filter, zero padded as for IMAX (assumed). Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.

effect_speaker_selection.doc: Effect speaker selection. Command format from the denonavr library (const.py, TelnetCommands); not yet tried on a receiver by this integration. Shown only when the receiver answers the query at setup.
